blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Agent harnesses are executable code that specifies the prompts, tools, and control flow around a language model. A single global harness can struggle with heterogeneous tasks that require different execution strategies. In this work, we introduce Object-Oriented Harness (OO-Harness), a harness optimization framework that evolves a hierarchy of executable harness classes using object-oriented design. During training, an evolution agent uses execution records to create a family of specialized harnesses, each implemented as a subclass of the base or an existing specialized harness via inheritance. At test time, a harness router uses routing lessons accumulated during training to select a specific harness for each task. Across three long-horizon benchmarks spanning business workflows, workspace tasks, and tool use, OO-Harness achieves the best performance among the compared methods, with an absolute improvement of up to 15% over the base. Extensive ablation studies examine the contributions of its core components.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Generalizing to tasks beyond the training distribution is a central goal
of language-agent research ( Zeng et al., 2023 ; Xi et al., 2024 ) .
Recent benchmarks illustrate the breadth of tasks agents must handle:
FutureX evaluates agents on forecasting real-world events using external
information ( Zeng et al., 2025 ) , while APEX-Agents evaluates
cross-application workflows in investment banking, management consulting,
and corporate law ( Vidgen et al., 2026 ) .
These workloads differ in the tool use, context management, and completion
checks they require. An agent’s harness implements these choices as
executable code around a language model ( Yang et al., 2024 ) .

Recent approaches automate agent design and harness optimization by
refining executable code and other harness components using execution
feedback ( Hu et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ; Lou et al., 2026 ; Lee et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026a ; Karten et al., 2026 ; Nie et al., 2026 ; Jiang et al., 2026 ) .
Meta-Harness, for example, evolves candidate programs using discovery-set
feedback and selects a global harness based on performance on that
set ( Lee et al., 2026 ) .
Such selection does not guarantee that the same changes remain beneficial
under distribution shift.
Even within a benchmark, Agentic Harness Engineering’s component ablations
show that adding evolved memory improves performance on hard tasks but
reduces it on easy ones ( Lin et al., 2026a ) .
EvoHarnessBench further shows that adding tools, skills, and specialist
agents can degrade previously effective behavior ( Ke et al., 2026 ) .
These findings motivate specialized harnesses that share common code while
preserving different execution strategies, with a router selecting a harness
for each task.

During training, we first cluster discovery tasks by shared execution
needs identified in base-harness execution records. An evolution agent iteratively selects a cluster and parent harness, creates a subclass,
and evaluates it across the cluster’s tasks. This feedback guides
subsequent revisions and accumulates as design and routing lessons.
This offers two advantages. Efficiency: evaluating candidates on
their target clusters avoids rerunning the entire discovery set. Generalization: specialized changes leave the base and other
learned harnesses intact, so new tasks can use an appropriate harness
without inheriting unrelated changes.
At test time, polymorphism allows the executor to run a selected
harness through a common execution interface. A harness router uses the task, an observable base trajectory, and routing lessons to
select a specialized harness or retain the base result. The hierarchy and lessons are frozen before deployment;
executor weights remain fixed in both phases.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Self-evolving agents use execution experience to improve prompts, memories,
skills, and other persistent components.
GEPA reflects on trajectories to optimize prompts ( Agrawal et al., 2025 ) ,
while ReasoningBank distills successful and failed experiences into reusable
memories ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) . A-Evolve considers deliberate
updates to persistent agent state ( Lin et al., 2026b ) , and HASP represents
skills as executable functions that modify actions or supply corrective
context ( Liu et al., 2026a ) . These forms of adaptation provide building
blocks for harness evolution. OO-Harness evolves specialized harnesses
through inheritance and uses a harness router to select one for each task.

blocks.en:
Recent work automates harness construction and revision through code search
and execution feedback, including Meta-Harness ( Lee et al., 2026 ) ,
Agentic Harness Engineering ( Lin et al., 2026a ) , and HarnessEvolve ( Jiang et al., 2026 ) . These approaches primarily optimize a global
harness across tasks, although changes that benefit one task group may not
benefit another. HarnessDev benchmarks harness creation and evolution ( Wu et al., 2026 ) , while EvoHarnessBench shows that expanding tools,
skills, and specialist agents can degrade previously effective behavior ( Ke et al., 2026 ) . Concurrent work explores adaptation across
tasks and deployments: Adaptive Auto-Harness shares and specializes workspace
contents through Git branching and rebasing ( Liu et al., 2026b ) , while EvolveNet
integrates adaptations from distributed deployments into a global harness ( Nie et al., 2026 ) . At the representation level, NOOA provides a
programming model that expresses agents as native Python objects ( Furgale et al., 2026 ) . OO-Harness evolves a hierarchy of executable harness
classes through inheritance, method overrides, and new methods. Its harness
router selects a harness using routing lessons accumulated during training,
class descriptions, the task, and an observable base trajectory.

In this section, we aim to understand the effectiveness of OO-Harness through

to relate execution needs to code and routing decisions
(§ 5.2 ). Finally, we construct an out-of-distribution (OOD) setting with
disjoint training and test application families, and examine Base reuse
on the selected test tasks (§ 5.3 ).

blocks.en: 5.3 Base harness reuse in OOD settings

blocks.en:
To examine behavior in extreme OOD scenarios, we construct a setting with 254
Toolathlon-GYM training tasks and 49 Toolathlon

disjoint, making the test set largely out of distribution relative to the
training set (Appendix A.7 ).
We evolve harnesses on this training split and compare OO-Harness against Meta-Harness .
At test time, Meta-Harness applies its learned global harness, whereas the OO-Harness router selects the general Base harness for every test task. As
Figure 7 shows, reusing Base preserves its performance,
while applying the Meta-Harness harness yields a lower PASS rate. Keeping Base
as a routing option allows OO-Harness to handle unfamiliar tasks without
requiring them to use a specialization learned on different application
families.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
OO-Harness evolves specialized harnesses through inheritance and
routes tasks using execution evidence. Task clusters capture shared execution
needs, and inheritance allows specialized harnesses to share useful code. OO-Harness achieves the best performance among baselines. Ablations support inheritance and trajectory-informed
routing, while case studies illustrate the effectiveness of specialization and Base reuse.

需要,而继承则允许专门技能者分享有用的代码。 OO-Harness在基线中取得了最佳业绩。 支持继承和了解轨迹
途径,而案例研究则说明了专业化和基地再利用的有效性。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
OO-Harness relies on the APIs and execution environment provided by its host.
Service outages and rate limits can affect reliability, while interface
changes may require updates to evolved harnesses. Integrating private or
authenticated services also requires secure credential handling and
permission configuration. These dependencies motivate further work on
robust API integration and deployment across environments.

变化可能需要对进化的带进行更新。 合并私人或
经认证的服务还需要可靠的证书处理和
权限配置。 这些依赖性促使进一步开展关于
强有力的API整合和跨环境部署.

blocks.en:
This ablation examines how an evolution step builds on previously learned
harness code. We compare three separate searches on Workspace-Bench, each
learning specialized harnesses for task clusters: • Base-reset (no code carry-over). Each candidate derives directly from Base. The evolution agent is asked
to implement one new mechanism without incorporating mechanisms from
earlier evolved nodes. Previous execution evidence and reflections remain
available to guide the proposal. Thus, each proposal starts afresh in its
code implementation while retaining the search’s diagnostic history. • Flat (copy-based reuse). Each candidate also derives directly from Base. When the target cluster
already has a deployed harness, the evolution agent is instructed to read
its source, copy all its accepted mechanisms into a new file, and then
add one new mechanism. The candidate cannot import, delegate to,
or inherit from other evolved nodes. Reuse therefore occurs through code
copied into the candidate, whose retained behavior is implemented within
the module. • OO (inheritance). The target cluster’s currently deployed harness becomes the candidate’s
parent; Base is used when the cluster has no specialist. The loader binds
this parent class to _Parent . Methods that the candidate does not
override remain inherited, while an override can call super() to
compose the parent’s behavior with a new change. The evolution agent can
inspect prior source, execution evidence, and reflections, then add a
specialized behavior without needing to copy the parent’s implementation.

blocks.en: Appendix B Case studies of specialized harnesses

blocks.en:
These cases show how OO-Harness turns execution needs into concrete code
changes and routing choices. We examine document generation on
Workspace-Bench, shared completion checks and routing lessons on
AutomationBench, and targeted runtime checks on Toolathlon-GYM.
blocks.zh:

改变和路由选择。 我们审查文件的生成
工作空间 -- -- 奔驰,共享完成检查和课程编排
自动奔驰 和定向运行时间检查 Toolathlon-GYM.

blocks.en: B.1 Workspace-Bench: generating Word documents
blocks.zh: B.1 工作空间-奔驰:生成 单词文档

blocks.en:
Document-writing tasks require both suitable content and a valid output
file. Writing plain text to a .docx path does not produce a Word
document. The office-doc-write harness addresses this problem
by wrapping the file backend and rendering supported text into a binary
Word document (Figure 8 ).
blocks.zh:
文件编写任务需要合适的内容和一个有效的输出
文档。 将纯文本写入.docx 路径不会生成 Word
文档。 办公室写字机能解决这个问题
通过将文件后端包裹,并将支持的文本渲染成二进制
单词文档(图8).

blocks.en:
The specialized backend handles direct document writes and can also
create a missing requested document from a text draft. In the latter
case, it preserves the original text write and leaves any existing
target document untouched. If rendering fails, execution falls back to
the parent backend. This capability handles the file format; the
benchmark separately evaluates whether the content satisfies the task.
blocks.zh:
专业后端处理直接文档写入,也可以
创建文本草稿中缺少的所请求的文档。 在后者中
语句,它保留了原始文本写入,并留下任何已有的
目标文档未激活。 如果渲染失败, 执行会回到
父后端。 此能力处理文件格式;
单独评估内容是否满足任务要求。

blocks.en:
The requested output format is often visible in the task description,
giving the router a useful cue for selecting this capability. This is
consistent with the small difference between task-only and
trajectory-based routing on Workspace-Bench.
blocks.zh:
请求的产出格式在任务描述中经常可见,
给路由器一个用于选择此能力的有用提示 。 这是
符合任务与任务之间的小差异
基于轨迹的路由 在工作空间-奔驰。

blocks.zh:

blocks.en: B.2 AutomationBench: inherited checks and routing lessons
blocks.zh: B.2 自动化奔驰:继承的检查和路由经验教训

blocks.en:
Business workflows often require changes to application state, but an
execution may finish after searching or reading without making an
update. An ancestor (s9) addresses this problem with a completion
check: when the task requires a write but no mutating API call has
occurred, it can request another turn.
blocks.zh:
业务工作流程往往需要更改应用程序状态,但
执行可在搜索或阅读后完成,而不制作
更新。 一个祖先(s9)通过完成解决这个问题
检查: 当任务需要写入, 但是没有变异 API 调用
发生了,它可以要求另一个转弯。

blocks.en:
Figure 9 shows successive extensions within the discovery-setup lineage. Building on s9’s missing-write
completion check, s12 adds a reminder near the turn limit when no
write has succeeded. Its child s29 retains both mechanisms and adds
guidance for unrecoverable errors and repeated unproductive tool results.
blocks.zh:
图9显示发现设置家族内连续的扩展. 以 S9 缺失的写法为基础
完成检查, s12 当无时在转弯限度附近添加提醒
写入成功 。 其儿童29岁保留了两种机制,并增加了
指导无法恢复的错误和重复的非生产性工具结果。

blocks.en:
Figure 9: Adding execution checks through inheritance. Successive nodes add a missing-write completion check, a near-budget
reminder, and tool-error guidance. Arrows show inheritance.
The filled node s29 is active; s9 and s12 are inactive ancestors
that supply inherited behavior.
blocks.zh:
图 9,通过继承方式增加执行检查. 连续节点添加一个缺失的写入补全检查, 一个近预算
教诲和引导。 箭头显示继承.
填充的节点 s29 活动; s9 和 s12 是不活动祖先
供给继承的行为。

blocks.en:
Routing lessons connect observed execution problems to harness
capabilities. For example, a lesson recommends an API error-normalizer
when an execution repeatedly encounters query-parsing errors. This
harness turns error feedback into instructions for repairing the query
(Figure 6 c).
blocks.zh:
总结经验教训,将观察到的执行问题联系起来,加以利用
能力。 例如,一个课建议一个 API 错误常态化器
当执行中再三遇到查询分析错误时。 这个
将错误反馈转换为用于修复查询的指令
(图6c).

blocks.en:
Table 4 gives two recorded routing choices.
An execution with no writes and repeated service errors is routed to a
resource-manifest harness, which supplies connected-service and resource
information to guide API exploration. A clean execution with successful
writes reuses Base. These examples show how lessons can select a
relevant intervention or preserve a clean Base execution.
blocks.zh:
表4提供了两个记录的路线选择。
执行时没有写和重复的服务错误会被引导到一个
提供连接服务和资源的有资源可支配的杠杆
指导API探索的信息. 处决成功
写入再利用 Base 。 这些例子表明,经验教训如何选择
相关干预或保持基地执行干净。

blocks.en: B.3 Toolathlon-GYM: refining when and what to check
blocks.zh: B.3 Toolathlon-GYM:何时和检查什么

blocks.en:
The learned clusters can span multiple applications
(Figure 10 ). For example, completeness-finalize includes tasks using Canvas, Notion,
Snowflake, and WooCommerce. The following examples show how evolution
refines a shared behavior and adds a check for a particular output.
blocks.zh:
学习的集群可以跨越多个应用程序
(图10). 例如,完整性的定稿包括使用Canvas,Notion,
雪花 还有WooCommerce 以下例子说明如何演变
完善共享行为并添加特定输出的检查.

blocks.en:
An ancestor of the completeness-finalize harness shortens
unusually long tool responses to limit the amount of text in the
execution history. Its child retains this behavior but adds an early-finish
condition: after an early completion attempt, any subsequent tool
outputs bypass compression. This allows the child to narrow when an
inherited intervention applies, using progress observed during execution.
blocks.zh:
完整完成的绳索的祖先缩短了时间
异常长的工具响应,以限制文本在
执行历史。 它的孩子保留了这种行为,但增加了一个早期的完成
条件: 提前完成尝试后, 任何后续工具
输出绕过压缩 。 这允许孩子在
利用执行过程中观察到的进展,适用继承干预。

blocks.en:
The excel-formula-literal harness adds a file check to inherited
guidance about writing computed values to spreadsheets
(Listing 1 ). Before finishing, it reads the saved workbook
and looks for cells with percentage labels and values strictly between
zero and one. It can then request one correction pass, listing the
identified cells and proposed values multiplied by 100.
blocks.zh:
优异的方格- literal 带增加了一个文件检查来继承
关于将计算值写入电子表格的指南
(表1)完成前,它会读到保存的工作手册
并查找带有百分比标签和数值的单元格
零和1个。 然后,它可以要求一份更正通行证,列出
已识别单元格和拟议值乘以100。

blocks.en:
This rule assumes that the task expects percentage points: for example,
20 rather than 0.2 for twenty percent. The instruction asks the executor
to change only the listed cells and preserve the rest of the workbook.
The harness therefore uses the contents of the produced file to decide
whether to request a targeted correction before finishing.
blocks.zh:
本规则假定任务预期百分比:例如,
20%而不是0.2%。 指令询问执行者
只更改列出的单元格,并保存工作手册的其余部分。
因此,利用生成文件的内容来决定
是否要求在完成之前进行有针对性的更正。
